title: Interest Is Owed on a Security Deposit
bodyText:
The city requires interest on a residential security deposit (B.R.C. 1981 sections 12-2-5 to 12-2-7). It is simple interest on the full deposit. The city manager sets the rate each December from one-year certificates of deposit and publishes it, and it applies to deposits provided in the next calendar year. For a tenancy of more than one year, figure the interest separately for each year, using the city's list of prior rates and its formula.

Return the accrued interest within one month after the lease ends or the home is surrendered and accepted, whichever is later, and follow state law on returning the deposit. If you don't give the notice state law requires for keeping a deposit, as to the interest, you lose the right to withhold any of the interest. Willfully and wrongfully keeping interest makes you liable for $100 or three times the amount kept, whichever is more, plus attorney's fees and court costs, if the tenant gave at least seven days' notice before filing. You carry the burden of proof. A lease term waiving any of this is void (section 12-2-8).

Exceptions: the ownership and return rules don't apply to a deposit paid to a mobile home park for a mobile home space. Under a lease entered into before March 19, 2004, the rate is 5.5 percent a year.
notes: B.R.C. 12-2-2, -5, -6, -7, -8 read whole 2026-11-25 (Taylor's download). Not checked: newer ordinances, the 2026 rate, state deposit deadline interplay. 12-2-7(a) first-year wording and (c) read together.

title: A Written Lease and Copies to Each Tenant
bodyText: If you rent residential property for 30 days or more, enter into a written lease within 30 days after the rental begins (B.R.C. 1981 section 12-2-3). Give each tenant a copy within seven working days after the lease is fully signed, or within fifteen working days after any tenant signs, whichever comes first. Before a summons is issued, the complaining witness or a city peace officer must first ask for a copy of the lease, and you then have five working days from the mailing or delivery of that request to provide it.

title: No Renting a Building Heated Only by a Solid Fuel Stove
bodyText: You may not rent out a building if a solid fuel burning device is its sole source of heat (B.R.C. 1981 sections 6-9-2 and 6-9-6). Sole source of heat means woodstoves are the only heating. A building doesn't count if it has a permanently installed furnace or heating system that uses oil, natural gas, electricity or propane, even one disconnected from its energy source. Any penalty falls on the owner, not the tenant.
notes: B.R.C. 6-9-1 to -6 read whole 2026-11-25. A disconnected system still isn't working heat under state habitability law: see parent row.

title: A Working Toilet and Sewage System Is the Owner's Duty
bodyText:
The owner of any structure where people live must make sure it has an adequate, convenient, sanitary toilet and sewage system in good working order, and sewage may not be discharged onto the ground or into state waters unless it meets the county's minimum requirements or state water quality standards, whichever apply (Weld County Code section 30-4-10). No one may maintain a dwelling without adequate facilities for disposing of sewage; a failed septic system doesn't count as adequate (section 30-4-140). Don't connect more than one dwelling to the same septic system unless the application and permit specified it.

The owner or occupant must let the county onto the property at reasonable times, on reasonable notice, to inspect a septic system (section 30-4-60).
notes: W.C.C. 30-4-10, -60, -140 read 2026-11-25. Reach inside cities not checked; chapter effective 2026-06-30 per 30-1-30.

title: Septic Maintenance Is the Owner's Unless a Contract Assigns It
bodyText: The county makes the owner responsible for maintaining a septic system unless a contract assigns that to a tenant, another party or a public body (Weld County Code section 30-13-10). The county rule allowing a contract doesn't settle whether state law lets a landlord shift the work: Colorado lets habitability repairs be moved to the tenant only in limited circumstances, so check the state rule first.
notes: W.C.C. 30-13-10 read whole 2026-11-25. State interplay (38-12-506) not re-read for septic.
